title: Mineral resource potential map of the Hell Hole Bay, Wambaw Swamp, Little Wambaw Swamp, and Wambaw Creek Wilderness, Berkeley and Charleston Counties, South Carolina
citation: Cameron, C.C., Grosz, A.E., Martin, C.M., and Gazdik, G.C., 1983, Mineral resource potential map of the Hell Hole Bay, Wambaw Swamp, Little Wambaw Swamp, and Wambaw Creek Wilderness, Berkeley and Charleston Counties, South Carolina: U.S. Geological Survey Miscellaneous Field Studies Map MF-1556-B, map scale 1:48,000.
notes: Mineral-resource pamphlet (pp. 1-9, text layer) and OCR plate (p. 11) repeating the text. Disagreements kept: PAH-23 clay at 34 to 60 ft (p. 5) vs at 34 ft, about 24 ft thick (p. 11); Upper Cretaceous-Paleocene section 2,000-2,400 ft (p. 3) vs 2,100-2,400 ft (p. 11); Santee age middle or middle and late Eocene (p. 3) vs late Eocene (p. 11). Heavy-mineral tables 3-4 recorded as auger-hole intervals; per-mineral percentages of table 3 and clay firing-test values not recorded. Peat sample depth 1 ft (CC82-1) has no bottom stated.
